articles.title: Travis Head hits back at Australia greats for firing a ‘bullet through’ current Test players
articles.summary: Opener said it is unfair for ex-players to criticise modern batting lineup. Australia’s vice-captain eager to open in Tests against South Africa. Travis Head has accused Australia’s golden generation of being unfair in “putting a bullet through” current players, saying the game has changed…
body: Just a day after Matthew Hayden slammed selectors and accused them of promoting “the greatest pile of mediocrity” after calling up Nic Maddinson, Head took his own stand in South Africa.
Australia’s vice-captain refused to make reference to particular critics or comments, but took issue with commentary around the team’s batting at a time when averages have dropped worldwide.
Head also noted the current side had been through a “sticky situation” with the group of past players, in a clear nod to Justin Langer’s dramatic exit as coach in 2022.

“I think it’s unfairly judged a fair bit from a group of past players, pretty much, that put the bullet through a lot of players,” Head said ahead of Friday’s first Test against South Africa in Durban.

articles.title: Eckert’s Spygate ban may be lenient, but no sane manager will try the same trick again
articles.summary: Verdict has been a long time coming and the Southampton head coach has recaptured hearts and minds at St Mary’s. “Hi Tonda, are you a cheat?” That simple, succinct, question cut to the heart of a matter that has vexed the Football Association all summer.
body: Although Southampton’s manager subsequently admitted to authorising spying on opponents, England’s football authorities struggled to decide what punishment best fitted an act some regard as heinous but which others fail to take seriously. Now, in autumn, we finally have an FA verdict, with Eckert given a six-week ban suspended until the end of the 2027-28 season, a £28,000 fine and a reprimand.
Despite the apparent leniency of the sanction, one thing is clear: Eckert’s summer in purgatory surely dictates no sane England-based coach would contemplate engaging in espionage now.

Eckert may wish he could turn back time to early May and rewrite history. On the eve of the playoff semi-final first leg on Teesside, William Salt, then an intern Southampton first-team analyst, was caught lurking awkwardly beside a tree while filming a Middlesbrough training session on his iPhone. Spygate was born and an independent disciplinary commission convened by the Football League (EFL) expelled Southampton from the playoff final against Hull after their win against Boro across two legs. The governing body also decreed the Saints would begin the current Championship season on minus four points.

articles.title: Jon Rahm’s LIV exit set to trigger mass exodus of players from stricken tour
articles.summary: Tyrrell Hatton and other big names likely to follow. Tour filed for bankruptcy after Saudi funding withdrawn. Confirmation that Jon Rahm will play no part in LIV Golf in its post-Saudi Arabian form is likely to be only the start of a mass exodus from the breakaway circuit.
body: A bankruptcy hearing on Wednesday heard Rahm’s lawyer say “unacceptable” terms proposed by LIV 2.0 mean the Spaniard will shortly walk away from a tour which has lingering hopes of continuing as a going concern. Rahm’s departure from LIV, which he joined in 2023, was inevitable, but still a significant blow and moment in time given his status in his sport.

“Mr Rahm has independently reviewed the proposed terms of LIV 2.0 and has determined that those terms are unacceptable to him and he will not be participating going forward in LIV 2.0,” the two-time major winner’s attorney, John Beck, said.

The expectation from those with knowledge of the LIV situation is that a batch of other players including Tyrrell Hatton, Tom McKibbin, Cameron Smith, Joaquin Niemann and Adrian Meronk will also flee the scene when legalities permit. The initial habitat for those players, from the start of next season, is likely to be the DP World Tour. LIV faces a race against time to earn commitment from players of even average quality in its mission to continue with 75-man events into 2027.

articles.title: Two icons, a glorious farewell and a potentially bitter ending
articles.summary: As Lionel Messi's international career ends in fond farewell, Cristiano Ronaldo's is at risk of petering out. BBC Sport takes a look at what could be the end of the international career's of two football greats.
body: On a night where one football legend received a grand farewell from his country, about 6,000 miles away, another released a lengthy statement discussing all the ways in which he had been wronged by his national team coach.
Argentina great Lionel Messi took the adulation of the crowd in Buenos Aires as his glittering international career ended with a goal against Benin on an emotional night.

Meanwhile, Portugal star Cristiano Ronaldo released a statement on social media, accusing manager Jorge Jesus of an "absolute breach of trust" while admitting he should be held accountable for his own actions.

The former Manchester United and Real Madrid forward left his country's Nations League camp last week after being an unused substitute against Norway and then finding out he would not start against Denmark.

articles.title: Texans Urged to Trade for Commanders Star After 0-4 Start
articles.summary: The Houston Texans have been urged to explore a trade for Washington Commanders defensive tackle Daron Payne after opening the 2026 season with an alarming 0-4 record.
body: Payne would give the Texans another powerful presence along the defensive line and could strengthen a unit that needs more consistency. His ability to disrupt opposing offenses from the interior would complement Houston’s existing pass rush while creating additional opportunities for its edge defenders to make plays.

The timing makes the potential move particularly intriguing because Houston cannot afford to waste another season with a roster capable of competing in the AFC. An 0-4 start creates an obvious sense of urgency, and acquiring a proven veteran could signal that the organization remains committed to turning the season around rather than shifting its attention toward the future.

There is also a financial component that Houston would need to consider before pursuing the deal. Payne is under a substantial contract, meaning the Texans would have to determine whether his expected production justifies the salary commitment and the draft capital Washington would likely seek in exchange for one of its most accomplished defensive players.

articles.summary: Former Tottenham defender Ramon Vega says he intends to run in next year's Fifa presidential election - becoming the first person to confirm they want to challenge Gianni Infantino.
body: Former Tottenham Hotspur defender Ramon Vega says he intends to stand as a candidate in next year's Fifa presidential election.
A former Switzerland centre-back, Vega also played for Celtic and Watford and has worked in finance since retiring from football in 2004.

"I am standing to reunite the global football family, deliver genuine and lasting reform, modernise Fifa for the 21st Century, restore stability and credibility, and rebuild the trust that our game urgently needs," he said.
Meanwhile, Sheikh Salman bin Ibrahim Al Khalifa - president of the Asian Football Confederation - has written to Infantino, distancing himself from an external review of Fifa's governance system.

articles.title: Report: LJ Martin out 4-6 weeks, will miss BYU-Notre Dame game
articles.summary: BYU’s injury luck continues to worsen. Star Cougars running back LJ Martin will miss the next four to six weeks with a lower body injury, according to a Wednesday report from Pete Thamel of ESPN.
body: The injury, which Martin sustained on his second carry against TCU last weekend, will sideline him for BYU’s nationally-televised prime-time matchup with Notre Dame on Oct. 17 in Provo.
BYU had already ruled Martin out for Friday’s game against Iowa State in its Big 12-mandated availability report released Tuesday night.

The reigning Big 12 Offensive Player of the Year, Martin has rushed for 344 yards and three touchdowns thus far in 2026, averaging 7.8 yards per carry. While he’s missed six games across the past three seasons due to various injuries, this current setback will likely be the longest health-related absence of Martin’s career.
Since debuting with the Cougars in 2023, Martin has racked up 2,885 yards on the ground to rank No. 6 all-time on the program leaderboard.

articles.title: Guardians survive with 9-3 win over White Sox
articles.summary: Jo Adell struck a bases-clearing triple as the Cleveland Guardians thumped the Chicago White Sox 9-3 Wednesday to stay alive in the Major League Baseball playoffs. Having lost two home games in the best-of-five series, Cleveland needed their own road win to avoid elimination -- and delivered in…
body: Chicago, hoping to clinch a playoff series at home for the first time since 1906, had fired up fans with a slender first-inning lead before a Steven Kwan single and Adell's triple sent Cleveland three ahead in the third.
The tenacious White Sox kept battling, as both sides leaned heavily on their bullpens, but could not rein in Cleveland before Jose Ramirez's two-run triple sealed the game.
"The approach was to get on base, try to put pressure on the other team with my speed, and make something happen. Thank God all those things came out well," said Ramirez.

The best-of-five American League Division Series continues Thursday in Chicago, where the White Sox have another chance to extend a fairytale year that has seen them bounce back from three straight 100-loss seasons to improbably reach the playoffs.

articles.title: Why Sprint in Singapore adds new twist to F1's toughest race
articles.summary: Formula 1 stages its sixth and final Sprint event of the year this weekend to conclude the first flyaway triple header of the sport's busy 2026 season run in.
body: And, for the first time, the Sprint format is being used at the Singapore Grand Prix and its Marina Bay street track, home of the sport's original night race.
But on a track not known for its overtaking, what kind of weekend can we expect with two qualifying sessions and two races?

When the Sprint format was first introduced at three races for the 2021 season, the tracks selected - Silverstone, Monza and Interlagos - were ones deemed to be particularly good for racing so to justify the addition of a 100km race on the Saturday as an appetiser to the main Sunday Grand Prix.
That has generally continued to be the case in the selection of Sprint venues up to this year, with perhaps the inclusion of Imola in 2022 the surprise exception.

articles.title: MotoGP Announces Reworked Race Weekend Format For 2027
articles.summary: Sprint race gets its own qualifying session. Photos by Yamaha. MotoGP race weekends are going to look different in 2027, and we're not just talking about the new 850cc engine displacement and Pirelli tires.
body: Starting next season, the grid for the Saturday Sprint races will be set by a dedicated 15-minute qualifying session on Friday afternoon, open to all riders. The Sunday race will have its own qualifying sessions. Until now, qualifying sessions on Saturdays set the grid for both races.

The reworked Friday opens with a 45-minute FP1, unchanged from the current format, followed by a 30-minute FP2 that replaces the hour-long Practice session. Critically, lap times in that FP2 no longer carry over to decide qualifying entry. The existing Practice served as the cut-off that sends the fastest 10 riders straight to Q2 and everyone else through Q1. Starting next season, Fridays will close with the new Sprint qualifying session.

Saturdays will begin with a 20-minute FP3, trimmed from the current 30 minutes, before Grand Prix qualifying. Every rider will take part in Q1, with the top 12 advancing to Q2. The Sprint then runs Saturday afternoon, with a grid established from Friday's qualifier.

articles.summary: Sergio Garcia is desperate to be involved in next year's Ryder Cup, either as a player or vice-captain, with his time on LIV Golf appearing to be coming to an end.
body: The Saudi-backed breakaway league filed for bankruptcy last month, with its restructuring plan likely to release players from their existing contracts ahead of a potential LIV 2.0 relaunch.
This week, Garcia successfully secured a court ruling to lift an automatic stay on his contract, allowing him to seriously consider his options for 2027.
Europe's all-time leading Ryder Cup points scorer now has his sights firmly set on Adare Manor next September.
"I think everything is an option," he told a press conference at the Open de Espana in Madrid.
